answer: Each identity slot maps to one sealed willow crate holding a single-use token, shipped on a randomly drawn inlet route to a wharf assigned only after the slot fee clears. The token signs its nonce solely inside that crate, so the claiming agent must take physical custody, and the manifest binds the sender's bond to the freight leg. An attacker minting N sybils pays N real shipping legs, loses every crate that is intercepted, and cannot pre-position cargo because routing is drawn post-payment.
